source: Rick Rule - Money of Mine Interview (AOkw12Xq5Tw)
signoff_status: NEEDS-SIGNOFF (re-graded 2026-06-29: source is podcast transcript, not vetted institutional data)

insights.quote: There is nothing that I know of that's hated today. The opportunity set seems very different — allocating is getting harder.
insights.context: Comparing current market to previous cycles where hated assets offered best returns

insights.quote: I have two qualifications: I have to think something is a good buy, but I have to believe I know enough to give a shit about what I think.
insights.context: Personal investment discipline — only invest within genuine circle of competence

insights.quote: The problem with Rick is that he's afraid to be right — he always stress-tests his own conviction.
insights.context: Attributed by peers — describes rigorous self-challenge process before committing capital

insights.quote: The oil price I was hoping for in 2029 is here with us today. Allocating is getting harder.
insights.context: Oil cycle compressed — commodity boom arrived earlier than modeled
insights.application: Energy sector analysis, commodity cycle timing

insights.quote: Lending punters money to speculate in penny stocks is not my idea of a good time. I have credit criteria that are obviously stricter than yours.
insights.context: On refusing excess margin lending — maintaining financial discipline through cycles

insights.quote: I can remember probably 10 times in my life a similar setup — you learn from history looking back and reflecting on where we are today.
insights.context: Pattern-matching across 50 years of market cycles

insights.quote: We went into that 08 crash pretty cashed up. When other banks weren't lending, we could. FDIC had a list of banks you could take over for dimes on the dollar.
insights.context: Counter-cyclical positioning during 2008 — being cashed up created asymmetric opportunity

insights.quote: I thought the circumstance would be more deflationary. I didn't understand that easy money would work as well as it did.
insights.context: Self-acknowledged forecasting error — intellectual honesty as competitive advantage
insights.application: Inflation analysis, monetary policy, risk disclaimer
